draft.title: Patterns of development
card: Development is how well people's lives are doing in terms of income, health and education. These differ greatly between countries, and also within a single country.
the value of goods and services a country produces in a year, divided by its population. It is an indicator of average income.
the Human Development Index combines income, life expectancy (health) and years of schooling (education) into one score between 0 and 1. A higher score means higher human development.
A national figure is an average, so it can hide gaps. Cities and regions in the same country can differ, for example in incomes or access to schools and hospitals.
draft.remember: Development is measured by indicators, and a national average can hide differences within a country.

a.q: Which pair of countries' scores shows that Country X has the higher level of human development?
opts: HDI of 0.92 for Country X and 0.55 for Country Y
HDI of 0.55 for Country X and 0.92 for Country Y
HDI of 0.30 for Country X and 0.70 for Country Y
HDI of 0.45 for Country X and 0.80 for Country Y
a.why: A higher HDI means higher human development, so 0.92 beats 0.55. The second option reverses this by giving the higher score to Country Y.
a.clue: On the HDI, is a higher score better or worse?

b.q: Country Z has a high GDP per person, yet people in its remote north have far shorter lives and less schooling than people in its capital. What does this show?
opts: A national average can hide differences within a country
GDP per person measures health and education directly
Development is the same everywhere within one country
The HDI cannot be calculated for a wealthy country
b.why: GDP per person is an average for the whole country, so it can hide gaps between regions. It measures only income, not health or education, which is why the second option is wrong.
b.clue: Think about what an average does to differences between places.

a.best: HDI of 0.92 for Country X and 0.55 for Country Y

b.best: A national average can hide differences within a country

problems.detail: Why (a) names 'the second option' as the reversal, but options are shuffled. In this order the reversal (0.55 for X, 0.92 for Y) is the third option, and the second (0.30 vs 0.70) is not a reversal. Describe the option by its content, not its position.

Why (b) refers to 'the second option' by position, which only works if the order is fixed. It also says GDP per person 'measures only income', but the card says GDP measures the value of goods and services produced and is an indicator of average income. Describe the distractor by content and match the card's wording.
Too easy for Year 11: all three wrong options give Country Y the higher score, so a student only has to spot the one pair where X's number is bigger.

Country Y produces more goods and services per person
Country X has more people, which lowers its HDI
Country X has the higher level of human development
